instruction: Use Chrome to access the Google Scholar citations page of the paper's corresponding author.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('f11'); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.scroll(-40)

metadata.explanation: Paraphrase using 'access' and 'citations page' terminology. The corresponding author is Tianlin (Tim) Shi (first author with correspondence email tianlin@cs.stanford.edu). The paper is 'World of Bits: An Open-Domain Platform for Web-Based Agents' from ICML 2017. Task requires identifying the corresponding author from PDF and navigating to their Google Scholar profile. Evaluator uses existing is_expected_url_pattern_match metric.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic correctly extracts active tab URL from accessibility tree
Metric correctly performs pattern matching on URL to verify both Google Scholar citations domain and specific author ID
Expected URL patterns are semantically correct - they identify both the Google Scholar citations page and the specific corresponding author (user=qRAQ5BsAAAAJ for Tianlin Shi)
Complete coverage of instruction requirements - verifies navigation to the correct citations page
Data flow is correct: accessibility tree → active URL → regex pattern matching
No postconfig needed despite heuristic warning - URL can be verified directly from accessibility tree without reopening UI
